rv.q: They bring the plays alive, brilliantly and made immediate
'Twelfth Night' is the centerpiece that gives the most chances for nuanced sexuality and comic delight.
Rylance is surrounded by a sublime company, who move seamlessly between the plays.
Rylance finds a way to go the extra yard as Olivia

Between bicycles, bongs, beatboxing, and buffoonery cranked to the max, playfulness rules in director Saheem Ali’s contemporary staging. That’s a viable approach to this 400-plus-year-old play — it’s a romantic comedy, after all. Nonetheless, like the richest rom-coms, Twelfth Night can cut deep when it matters most.
For a comedy that's about characters carried away by sexual desire, there's surprisingly little warmth in this 'Twelfth Night.'

A triumphant gender-defying curtain call, costumed in glorious technicolor by Oana Botez, further challenges the recent assault on creative expression and the arts, demonstrating that joy is an act of resistance.
The production is pretty well-cast all around.
